findings.title: Sigma-10 JP credit preview notice forces mobile horizontal document overflow
findings.source_fragment: .creditRate::before { content: '\30d7\30ec\30d3\30e5\30fc\6642...'; display: list-item; font-weight: bold; margin: 1.5em 0; white-space: pre; }
findings.observed_behavior: At 390px the document scrollWidth is 503 (chromium and firefox) / 492 (webkit); at 320px it is 500. The ~478px single-line ::before content cannot wrap because white-space:pre, so ul.creditRate overflows and expands the document. Sigma-9 runtime baseline on the identical page and shell keeps documentWidth at 390.
findings.expected_behavior: The credit notice should wrap (or be scoped to preview) so no document-level horizontal overflow occurs at supported narrow widths.
findings.why_sigma10_not_wikijump: The overflow appears only when the Sigma-10 replacement CSS is applied; the identical DOM under the runtime Sigma-9 baseline measures 390. Removing ul.creditRate from the same Sigma-10 DOM drops documentWidth 511->390 (isolated probe). The rule and its white-space:pre are Sigma-10 JP localization source.
findings.minimal_recommended_change: Change the notice to white-space: pre-wrap (or normal), and scope the notice+'.creditRate > li{display:none}' rule to the preview context only if that was the intent.

theme_impact.note: Document width equals ul.creditRate reachable_right for every theme that overflows; contained themes clip it and keep documentWidth 390.

findings.title: Sigma-10 hides the desktop search input, removing a working Wikijump search entry
findings.source_fragment: #search-top-box-input { display: none; }  /* comment: 'Commenting out the search box at the top while native Wikidot search remains non-functional.' */
findings.observed_behavior: The desktop shell.search.typed-focused state fails closed because #search-top-box-input is not visible. The submit button remains.
findings.expected_behavior: Wikidot parity: hidden (native Wikidot search is non-functional). Wikijump consequence: Wikijump search is functional, so hiding the input removes the primary search entry on Wikijump.
findings.why_sigma10_not_wikijump: The hiding rule is Sigma-10 baseline CSS, inherited from upstream. Wikijump exposes a working search (submitWikidotTopSearch).
findings.minimal_recommended_change: Decide whether SCP-JP wants a search entry on Wikijump; if so, re-enable #search-top-box-input for the Wikijump environment or override it in the SCP-JP shell.

evidence.audit_record: sigma10-baseline / chromium / desktop / shell.search.typed-focused (UNCONFIRMED, action/capture failed: #search-top-box-input not visible)

findings.title: Migration shell injection was silently reverted by Svelte hydration
findings.description: The source-derived #top-bar/#side-bar substitution ran immediately after DOMContentLoaded, but the Svelte shell hydrates ~1.3 s later and re-rendered the stale Theme Lab acceptance navigation over it. Until fixed, every migration nav/shell state measured the retired Sigma-9 acceptance shell rather than the Sigma-10 SCP-JP shell.
findings.evidence: Captured DOM before the fix contained Theme Lab navigation; after the fix #side-bar contains the Sigma-10 nav-side (初めての方へ) and #top-bar contains the Sigma-10 nav-top ([# SCPデータベース]).
findings.fix: capture-interactive.mjs injectMigrationShell() now waits for a delegated Svelte handler as a hydration barrier and re-applies the substitution until it survives a 400 ms quiet window, failing hard if it never stabilises.

findings.title: Interwiki visible contract depends on external crom/Interwiki services not available offline
findings.description: Wikijump's local interwikiFrame route emits style="display:none" when the external crom GraphQL fetch (api.crom.avn.sh) is blocked, so .scpnet-interwiki-frame has no links/height. The state fails closed (UNCONFIRMED) instead of producing a false PASS. The Sigma-10 nav-side/nav-interwiki/styleFrame includes also reference external scp-jp.org frames.
findings.evidence: chromium desktop+mobile shell.interwiki.visible: action/capture failed: .scpnet-interwiki-frame not visible.

findings.title: Migration content/shell state fixture binding
findings.description: nav.* and shell.* states now bind to the migration-owned run-owned:sigma10-main page (Sigma-10 SCP-JP shell) rather than the retired acceptance page. Content-component states (content.tabview, content.collapsible), credit.*, and page history/source/files/tags/edit states keep the Theme Lab acceptance fixture because the frozen Sigma-10 example main page does not contain those components; the Sigma-10 baseline CSS is still applied to them.
findings.evidence: See audit records: nav.* / shell.* fixture = run-owned:sigma10-main; content/credit/page.* fixture = run-owned:theme-lab-visual-acceptance-imported-20260924.

unresolved_simulator_limitations: Interwiki visible/style contract cannot be evaluated offline (external crom + scp-jp.org frames); shell.interwiki.visible fails closed.

Semantic/visual review (readability, keyboard/focus order, pointer/hover, modal reachability) is not complete for every state; geometry and overflow are captured but classification remains UNCONFIRMED where not reviewed.
Local development runtime is shared with a concurrent deepwell mutation-testing session and recompiled repeatedly during this run; captures that caught a restart window were retried.
Authenticated admin surfaces captured on chromium desktop+mobile only.

WebKit theme runs report one missing decorative external asset (scp-jp.github.io/.../nav/side/black.png from the Sigma-10 nav-side close-menu overlay); it is blocked by network policy, is not in the frozen dependency snapshot, and does not change the close-menu geometry. Chromium/Firefox block it silently.
Theme matrices cover chromium desktop + chromium/firefox/webkit mobile + chromium narrow-mobile; firefox/webkit desktop and narrow-mobile theme matrices are not run.
intentional_differences: Sigma-10 header hides the configured site title/tagline text (max-height:0; line-height:0). The visible "Local Translation Corpus" text is the local test site configuration, not SCP-JP source; production SCP-JP would supply its own title/tagline.
Sigma-10 baseline intentionally hides #search-top-box-input for Wikidot parity (see SIGMA10-SEARCH-002 for the Wikijump consequence).
Theme overlays change document typography, so the credit notice width (and therefore overflow magnitude) differs per theme; this is a consequence of SIGMA10-MOB-001, not a separate theme defect.
